The Petitioner has made an elaborate submission of background, circumstances that necessitate the Respondent No.2 to issue the Section 11 directions, which is not covered in this order for the sake of brevity and convenience. Relevant submissions with regard to the dispute of payment are referred to as under:- d) The Petitioner submits that the benchmark tariff notified by the Respondent No.2 was insufficient, but the Petitioner continued to supply the power to the Respondent No.1, as per the benchmark tariff notified by the Respondent No. 2 vide various directions. The Petitioner has approached this Commission vide Petition No. 162/MP/2022, seeking recovery of the actual cost over and above the benchmark tariff notified by the Respondent No.2. h) The Petitioner submits that they supplied the power as per the terms of the directions to the Respondent No.1. However, the Respondent No.1 e) The Respondent No.2, on 19.12.2022, replied to the Petitioner’s letter dated 25.11.2022, directing both the Petitioner and the Respondent No. f) The Petitioner has failed to place evidence with respect to the dispute that the Respondent No. 1 has procured imported coal 45-60 days in advance for supply in the month of December 2022. The invoices raised for the sale of coal upon the Petitioner suggest that the Petitioner has been procuring coal domestically from India-based vendors. Petitioner has acted in derogation of the directions of the MoP under Section 11, as the Petitioner neither pleaded nor demonstrated its efforts to sell power in the exchanges, upon the Respondent’s refusal to procure power at the MoP pass-through tariff. g) The Respondent No.1 has raised the issue of jurisdiction on the ground that there is no composite scheme exists, as the Respondent No.1 is the sole procurer, as there is no inter-state supply of power from the Petitioner’s power plant, and the Petitioner only has a tie-up for the supply of power to the Respondent No. 1 under the existing PPA. The b) The Petitioner submits that the directions issued by the Respondent No.2 which are statutory in nature, have resulted in modification of the terms of PPA executed between the Petitioner and the Respondent No.1. Therefore, the Respondent No.1, being one of the parties to the - d) The Petitioner submits that this Commission, vide its Record of Proceedings in the Petition No. 350/MP/2022, clarified that the Respondent No.2’s directions were applicable until 31.12.2022, and any action of the Respondent No.1 shall be subject to the final outcome of the case. g) The Petitioner submits that the instant Petition is very well within the jurisdiction of the Commission due to the fact that the directions under Section 11(1) were issued by the Central Government (through MoP) upon all the imported coal-based power plants, wherein the power plant of the Petitioner was specifically identified and was mandated in terms of the said directions to supply power to the Respondent No.1, and/ or in the Energy Exchanges. The Petitioner further submits that the transactions during the period when the power was supplied by the Petitioner to the Respondent No.1 in terms of the MoP’s directions were nothing but inter-state generation, and as a result, this Commission only has the jurisdiction to entertain the present petition. In this regard, the Petitioner has referred to the order passed by the Commission in the Petition No. 351/MP/2018, Coastal Energen Private Ltd. v. TANGEDCO & Ors. 10. The matter was heard on 10.5.2023, 20.3.2024 and 22.8.2024. The Petition was admitted vide Record of Proceedings of the hearing dated 10.5.2023, and after hearing the submissions of the Petitioner, the Commission admitted the matter and directed the parties to file their respective replies and rejoinders, if any. The Respondent No.1, vide its written submissions dated 13.11.2023, has mainly reiterated its submissions in its reply; therefore, the same is not repeated . The Petitioner also made its written submissions on 3.11.2023, reiterating its earlier submissions. In case of the any grievances in relation to the charges to be payable by/receivable from TANGEDCO for such supply by the Petitioners during the subsistence of direction of MoP, the Petitioners are at liberty to approach the Commission with fresh Petitions and contentions of both the sides, on these aspects, are kept open. title: Petition under Section 79 and Section 11(2) of the Electricity Act, 2003 read with Regulation 111-113 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Conduct of Business) Regulations, 1999 seeking recovery of energy charges for the power procured in the month of December, 2022, in terms of the directions issued by the Ministry of Power, Government of India under Section 11 of the Electricity Act, 2003.
